answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through a scarce, time-locked stake: each identity must escrow tokens before it can certify a transaction, and the stake is slashed if later evidence proves fraud. Splitting the same funds across a thousand umber, juniper, or timber-named accounts adds no weight, because votes are capped by stake, not account count. A sybil attacker must therefore lock substantial capital and risk losing it, while honest agents can build influence gradually through accountable participation.
